clue.text: 24 23down's friend's adaptation of the cupboard under the stairs?

definitions.meaning: a companion of the outlaw from crossing entries 24 and 23, the big man of his band of merry men

definitions.text: adaptation of the cupboard under the stairs?
definitions.meaning: a whimsical name for a small lavatory squeezed into the space beneath a staircase, john being slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone converts the understairs cupboard for a famous outlaw's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after friend reads as 'is': the companion is also a little toilet. JOHN is slang for a lavatory, and a cramped downstairs loo is often a converted understairs cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw's giant lieutenant is ironically nicknamed for being small, and a tiny lavatory is jokingly a little john.

clue.text: Snapper takes the middle of the film in colour

indicators.note: in places the letters from the film inside the colour word

parts.note: bluish is a colour, a shade tending to blue

indicators.note: the middle of the phrase the film is where its two words meet, giving the letters either side of the join

explanation.surface: A snapper picks up a central role in a colour film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' takes the letters at the centre of 'the film', the end of THE and start of FILM, giving EF; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluefish is a predatory sea fish known in Australia and elsewhere as a snapper or tailor.

clue.text: See 8
See 21 across
Such as Calypso is wanted in dance

indicators.note: dance suggests the letters jigging about into a new order

explanation.surface: A calypso singer is in demand to play at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Calypso looks like the Greek nymph, but here it is the Caribbean song style, which comes from the West Indies; 'dance' rearranges IS WANTED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso music originated in Trinidad, so it is an example of something Caribbean in origin.

clue.text: Home of 24 23down, a crock about court, sick of repose

indicators.note: about means the broken-pottery word goes round the wooing word

parts.note: a sherd is a broken piece of crockery, a fragment of a crock
to court a sweetheart is to woo

indicators.note: being sick brings things up, and in a down clue that turns the little word upwards

parts.note: repose means rest

explanation.surface: An old wreck at court, tired of rest, describes the outlaw's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' signals a reversal: being sick brings things up, and this is a down clue. 'a crock' is fair because a sherd (shard) is a broken bit of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nottinghamshire woodland is the legendary hideout of the outlaw and his band.

clue.text: With the passage of the hours wine finds me with bad boys, for example

definitions.text: With the passage of the hours

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
taken as written

indicators.note: bad suggests the boys are messed up into another order

explanation.surface: As time passes, a drinker finds himself in the company of bad boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles BOYS together with EG (for example) to give GOES BY. The answer is the song from Casablanca.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title phrase describes time passing, which is what the clue's opening words say.

clue.text: 24 23down's friend writing awfully dim song when he's around

indicators.note: around means the man word encloses everything else

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are jumbled badly

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: The outlaw's friend writes a terribly dull song whenever he is about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' makes AIDMARIA from the dull word plus the song, and 'around' signals the enclosure; 'writing' and 'when' are links, and 'he' standing for a man is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw's sweetheart in the legends is a maiden of that name.

clue.text: I haven't much of 11 16 until real trouble occurs

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be short of compassion only when real trouble happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges UNTIL REAL; 'occurs' is a link. The definition is a cryptic self-description: someone lacking kindliness has this temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: A person short of compassion has a spiteful disposition, the opposite of kindliness.

clue.text: The entertainer's article is a plant

parts.note: a host entertains guests
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A party host's piece of writing turns out to be about a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostas are shade-loving garden plants grown for their broad leaves.

clue.text: I find folk wild and barbarian, including the generality of folk, amid the chaos — Macbeth must have spilt it!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: amid puts the long string inside the word for chaos

parts.note: a mess is chaos
taken as written

indicators.note: wild means the letters of folk run riot
including means the barbarian word holds the people word

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders
people in general, the whole human race

explanation.surface: A tirade about savage folk in the midst of disorder ends with a nod to Shakespeare's Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' gives LKOF; 'including' and 'amid' signal the two enclosures. Lady Macbeth fears her husband is 'too full o' the milk of human kindness', so a murderer must have spilt it.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer like Macbeth must have lost the compassion Lady Macbeth says he is too full of.

clue.text: Fellow in blue and red keeping one staid, they say

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, a fellow in navy blue

indicators.note: keeping means red holds the numeral inside

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man dressed in blue and red is keeping someone respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken: 'staid, they say' sounds like stayed. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lingered or remained somewhere is to have stayed, which sounds like staid.

clue.text: Return of the unsophisticated spa

indicators.note: return means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: naive means unsophisticated

explanation.surface: Unsophisticated visitors come back to the spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Évian-les-Bains is a French spa town famous for its mineral water.

clue.text: Stick around — sounds uttered in China

indicators.note: around means the stick word encloses the sounds

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
tones are sounds

explanation.surface: Someone with a stick hears sounds spoken in China.
explanation.walkthrough: Cantonese is a tonal language, so 'sounds' doubles neatly with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is a Chinese language spoken in Guangdong and Hong Kong.

clue.text: Dean (the 21 down)'s new friend featured in binder

indicators.note: featured in puts the scrambled letters inside the binder word

parts.note: cord binds things together

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A new friend of a college dean appears in a ring binder.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean is not a college officer but the Forest of Dean; the 's means 'is': the answer is a town there. 'new' rearranges FRIEND into INDERF.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderford is a market town within the Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire.

clue.text: Here's Beverley, with an awkward seat on a horse

indicators.note: awkward hints that the letters sit badly and must be rearranged

parts.note: riding means being on a horse

explanation.surface: Beverley sits awkwardly in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Beverley looks like a woman's name but is the county town of the East Riding of Yorkshire, an English county area.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverley is the administrative centre of that Yorkshire division, so it is located there.

clue.text: See 11
A lot of money gets meagre return when celebrity comes in

indicators.note: comes in means the celebrity enters the reversed word
return means meagre's synonym is read backwards

parts.note: slim means meagre, as in slim chances
a lion is a celebrity, a social lion

explanation.surface: Big money brings small returns once a star gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' makes MILS; 'comes in' signals the enclosure. A social lion is an old word for a much-sought-after celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Millions is an informal word for a vast sum, a fortune.

clue.text: English soldier turns up in hymn, close to the soil

indicators.note: in places the turned soldier inside the hymn

parts.note: a paean is a hymn of praise

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An English soldier appears in a hymn about the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' gives IG, since a down clue reads upwards; 'in' signals the enclosure. Epigaean is a rare botanical word, so the wordplay does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigaean is a botanical term for growing on or near the surface of the ground.

clue.text: Boxer constructs a ginnel round a hill

indicators.note: round means the rearranged alley letters go about the hill
constructs suggests building something new from the letters

parts.note: ben is a Scottish mountain or hill

explanation.surface: A boxer builds an alley around a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A ginnel is a northern English word for a narrow alley between houses. 'constructs' gives NIGELN, and 'round' signals the enclosure; the 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Benn was a British middleweight and super-middleweight world champion boxer.

clue.text: See 7
The chap at the chippy reportedly has food for 24 23down's friend

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a chippy is a fish-and-chip shop, whose cook is the fryer
tuck is British slang for food, especially schoolboys' snacks

explanation.surface: The chip-shop man has a meal for the outlaw's companion.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is a British fish-and-chip shop; the fryer there sounds like FRIAR. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The jovial portly monk is one of the outlaw's band of merry men.

clue.text: See 6
The lady with a piece of music was 24 23down's enemy

parts.note: she refers to a lady
a riff is a short repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: A lady with a tune was the outlaw's foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'was' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sheriff of Nottingham is the outlaw's arch-adversary in the legends.

clue.text: The rise of love is painful

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Eros is the god of love

explanation.surface: Love's growth hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore means aching or tender, so it describes something that hurts.

clue.text: Cambridge University's tough for a vicar without energy to get in

indicators.note: to get in means the vicar piece enters the tough word

parts.note: hard means tough

indicators.note: without means the energy letter is dropped

parts.note: Rev is short for a reverend, a vicar
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Cambridge University is hard for a vicar lacking energy to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge is not the English one: Harvard is in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The 's means 'is'; 'for' is a link. ARV goes inside HARD after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard University stands in Cambridge, Massachusetts, across the river from Boston.

clue.text: See 24
Wouldn't he show his face when he stole?

definitions.text: Wouldn't he show his face when he stole?

parts.words: Wouldn't he show his face when he stole?
parts.note: a thief would keep his face covered while stealing, robbing in a cowl, which splits the outlaw's name

explanation.surface: A question about whether a thief hides his face.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the name as 'rob in hood': a robber wearing a hood hides his face.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw robbed the rich, and his name splits into a description of a hooded robber.

clue.text: Bird's eggs can be moved up the side

definitions.text: can be moved up the side

parts.note: a rook is a crow-like bird, and the possessive keeps its S
spawn is the eggs of fish or frogs

explanation.surface: A bird's eggs can be shifted up the side of the nest.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the rook's pawn stands on the edge file and advances along the side of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook's pawn starts on the a- or h-file, at the board's edge, and moves up along it.
